scenes.vo: Back to the Keeper. Episode one: when do we go back? A pass back to your keeper can be the smartest pass on the pitch, if you pick the right moment.

steps.heading: When to go back
steps.sub: Facing our goal. Attacker close. Nothing safe forward.
steps.vo: Step one. When do we go back? Check three things. Are you facing our own goal? Is an attacker close behind you? Is there nothing safe going forward? Then go back to your keeper.

steps.heading: Turn when you can
steps.sub: Space and time? Turn and play forward.
steps.vo: Step two. If the attacker is far away and you have time, turn and play forward. Going back every time makes us easy to press. Check over your shoulder before the ball arrives, so you already know which one it is.

steps.heading: Back keeps the ball
steps.sub: Your keeper is an extra player. Then we start again.
steps.vo: Step three. Going back is not giving up. It keeps the ball, and your keeper becomes an extra player. The attacker has to chase all the way back, and we can start again on the other side.

steps.heading: Be the way out
steps.sub: See it early. Get open to the side. Call "Yes!"
steps.vo: Keepers, when you see a team-mate facing our goal with an attacker behind, that's your cue. Get off your line, get open to the side, and call yes, nice and loud.

scenes.label: Napoli v Man City, keeper Ederson

beats.vo: First, how it's done. Napoli against Manchester City. City's defender, number 30, has the ball near his own box, facing his own goal, and a Napoli forward is chasing him.
He has two choices. One: turn and dribble up the line. Two: pass it back to his keeper, Ederson, out by the side of the goal.
Back to the keeper. If he turns, the forward is right there. Ederson is off his line and out to the side, ready for it. That's a safe pass, away from the forward.
Stop. Now the forward is chasing Ederson. His choices: one, a short pass to his team-mate on the left. Two, kick it long, up the pitch.
Both are safe. His team-mate on the left is open, with no one near him, so the short pass keeps the ball. Ederson doesn't wait for the forward to arrive. One touch, and pass it to the open player.
The forward slides in and misses. City keep the ball. A firm pass back to the side, a keeper who's ready out wide, and a quick pass to the open player. That's how it's done.
beats.caption: Back to the side. Keeper ready. Find the open player.

beats.vo: Now one where it went wrong, so we can learn from it. A Premier League game. A long ball goes over the defence. Watch the defender, in light green, chasing it back toward his own goal.
Stop. The defender gets there first, but he's facing his own goal. He has three choices. One: turn up the line. Two: pass inside to his midfielder. Three: pass it back to the keeper.
Back to the keeper. Turning, the striker is right on his shoulder. Inside, his midfielder is running toward our goal too. The keeper can see the whole pitch. Watch what he does.

Good choice. Now you're the keeper. This is his view, and the striker is closing him down. Your choices: one, the midfielder in the middle. Two, the midfielder on the right. Three, the defender who just passed it, out wide, off the picture to the right. Four, kick it long.

One, three and four are all good. The midfielder in the middle is open. The defender out wide is free. Kicking it long is safe. Two is the risky one: the midfielder on the right has an opponent right next to him. Watch what he did.
He played it in between them, toward the covered player. It was cut out, and they scored. Keepers: pick the open player, or kick it long. Defenders: after you pass back, get open again.
beats.caption: After you pass back, get open again.

annotations.text: His pass: toward the covered player

scenes.note: Turn and play forward. Check over your shoulder before the ball arrives.
scenes.vo: Remember the three checks. Facing our goal? Attacker close? Nothing safe forward? Then go back. If you have space and time, turn and play forward. Turn, or return.
